# CANDIDATE: NAMED_LEVEL_SWEEP_WICK_REVERSAL

**Filed:** 2026-09-08  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger

## Hypothesis

A brief sweep beyond a prior‑day high/low that closes back inside the level with a rejection wick often precedes a reversal in the opposite direction. This captures mean-reversion momentum after false breakouts, exploiting retail FOMD and institutional stop hunts at named levels.

## Mechanism

Define prior‑day high (PDH) and low (PDL). For a short: if high > PDH × 1.002 (0.2% sweep) AND close < PDH AND (high – close) > 0.6 × (high – low) (long upper wick), go short at close. For a long: mirror logic using PDL with a long lower wick. Exit shape: Stop = extreme of the sweep (high for short, low for long); target = opposite named level (PDL for short, PDH for long) or 1.5R, whichever is reached first. Regime hint: Best in middling volatility (VIX between 15‑25) and when the prior‑day range is not excessively tight (PDH‑PDL > 0.3% of SPY).
